current.text: Johnson is a rookie. Dallas drafted him with a top 10 pick.
Johnson is hurt now. Yahoo lists him as questionable with a lower leg injury. Lively is also hurt.
Because Johnson and Lively are hurt, Daniel Gafford is the likely opening night center.
The Dallas frontcourt is crowded. Lively, Gafford, Powell, P.J. Washington and Aldama all compete for big man minutes.
Dusty May is the new head coach. It is unknown how he will split minutes among the centers.
Josh makes Johnson his late swing pick over P.J. Washington in standard formats. His upside is 30 minutes a night with about 12 points, 9 rebounds, 1.5 blocks and 1 steal.
Experts see him as a reasonable late flyer. One ranks him around 150 on 25 minutes a night. Josh says his low Fantrax ADP of 209 may mean there is value.
Dallas has a 4-4-4 schedule in the fantasy playoffs, probably the best in the league. It also has a league-high 16 back-to-backs.

durable.text: Johnson is an undersized, hard-working energy big at 6'9. His motor is his main strength. He fits better as a four than a five.
He had strong defensive stats at Michigan and in Summer League. He had one of the best lateral quickness measurements at the combine.
He rebounds, finishes well and scores on mismatches in the post.
His shooting is a question. He shot some threes in college and Summer League, but experts do not see him as a real stretch big. It is also unclear whether he can create his own usage.

note: Both sites give him a value of 0 USD (Yahoo rank 208, ESPN rank 166), so he sits at the edge of our 144-player pool. At most he is a 1 USD late flyer for blocks and FG%. The two projections also disagree on his FG% (58.9 vs 49.4). Before the draft on 2026-10-18, check his lower leg injury and the Lively timeline. Early in the season, watch whether Dusty May starts him at center over Gafford. If he gets 25 to 30 minutes, he is worth a waiver pickup, and the Dallas 4-4-4 playoff schedule helps.
